title: Victims Say Rex Ryan’s Truck “Almost Killed” Them in Nashville Crash, NBC Sports Reports
body:
The victims of a high‑speed crash on Nashville’s Interstate 40 last week have filed sworn statements accusing former NFL head coach Rex Ryan of reckless driving that nearly cost them their lives. According to the affidavits obtained by local authorities, Ryan was operating a black 2022 Chevrolet Silverado when he allegedly accelerated through a stopped traffic queue, forced his way into a lane occupied by a line of stopped cars, and struck a convoy of three vehicles, injuring all occupants. The statements, which were released to the public by the Nashville Police Department, allege that Ryan’s actions constituted “gross negligence” and “willful endangerment,” prompting calls for criminal charges and a civil lawsuit.

The incident occurred shortly after 5 p.m. on Thursday, when a traffic jam caused by construction work forced drivers onto the shoulder of the highway. Witnesses say Ryan’s truck appeared from a side road, revved its engine, and surged forward, ignoring the stopped traffic. The impact left one passenger with a broken wrist, another with a concussion, and a third with whiplash. All three victims were taken to Vanderbilt University Medical Center for treatment and released later that night, but they have since decided to pursue legal action. Their attorneys, a Nashville‑based firm specializing in personal‑injury litigation, filed a complaint on Friday alleging that Ryan “operated his vehicle with a conscious disregard for the safety of others” and that his conduct “constitutes a criminal act under Tennessee law.”

Ryan, who retired from coaching in 2022 after a 15‑year tenure that included stints with the New York Jets and Buffalo Bills, has not yet commented publicly on the allegations. His legal team, however, released a brief statement indicating that “Mr. Ryan is cooperating fully with law enforcement and will vigorously defend against any unfounded claims.” The statement also noted that Ryan was not under the influence of any substances at the time of the crash, a point that has been a focal concern for investigators.

Legal experts say the case could hinge on whether prosecutors can prove that Ryan’s behavior rose above ordinary negligence to a level that justifies criminal charges such as reckless driving or even vehicular assault. “Tennessee law defines reckless driving as operating a vehicle with a wanton or willful disregard for the safety of persons or property,” explains Professor Linda Martinez, a criminal law scholar at Vanderbilt University. “If the evidence shows that Ryan intentionally accelerated through a stopped line, that could meet the statutory threshold.” The victims’ attorneys argue that the driver’s sudden acceleration and failure to heed traffic signals constitute exactly that level of disregard.

The incident also revives a broader conversation about the conduct of high‑profile athletes and coaches off the field. In recent years, several former professional sports figures have faced legal scrutiny for alleged dangerous driving, ranging from DUI offenses to hit‑and‑run incidents. Critics argue that the celebrity status and wealth of such individuals sometimes foster a sense of entitlement that can translate into risky behavior behind the wheel. “When public figures act with impunity, it sends a dangerous message to the community,” says Dr. Michael Greene, a sociologist who studies celebrity culture. “Accountability is essential, not just for the victims, but for the broader public perception of fairness under the law.”

As the investigation proceeds, Nashville police have indicated that they will review dash‑cam footage, traffic camera recordings, and the truck’s telematics data to reconstruct the events leading up to the crash. A hearing on the potential filing of criminal charges is scheduled for early next month, and the civil suit is expected to move forward in the Nashville Circuit Court shortly thereafter. The outcomes of both proceedings could set a precedent for how the legal system addresses reckless conduct by high‑profile individuals.

Regardless of the legal resolution, the victims’ families hope their case will serve as a warning to all drivers about the perils of aggressive behavior on congested roadways. “We never imagined a former coach would put us in this position,” said one of the injured parties, who asked to remain anonymous. “We just want to make sure no one else has to go through what we did.” The coming weeks will reveal whether justice will be served through criminal prosecution, civil compensation, or a combination of both, and will likely influence how similar incidents are handled in the future.
